members.name: cointegration_pairs_v1
members.thesis: Cointegrated stock pairs identified via Engle-Granger two-step procedure exhibit stronger mean-reversion properties than simple correlation-based pairs. By running a rolling cointegration test on 5-day intraday data (1500+ bars) and only trading pairs where the ADF test on residuals rejects the unit
members.exit_stop: z_score exceeds 3.5 OR loss > 0.6% of capital
filters: India_VIX < 22; PSU bank vol spikes in high-VIX environments
SBIN 1-min vol > 50000 shares, PNB > 100000 shares at entry
weaknesses: PSU banks are subject to government policy shocks (merger announcements, capital infusion) that can permanently shift the cointegration relationship without warning
PNB has lower liquidity and wider spreads than SBIN, causing asymmetric slippage: the PNB leg often fills worse, creating persistent small drag on returns
Rolling cointegration using 5-day data (1500 bars) is computationally expensive and may lag genuine structural breaks by several hours
members.prior_art: Engle & Granger (1987) cointegration; Vidyamurthy (2004) cointegration-based pairs trading. Alexander & Dimitriu (2005) for rolling cointegration window calibration.

members.name: cointegration_residual_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 50 constituent pairs within same GICS sector (e.g., HDFCBANK-ICICIBANK, TCS-INFOSYS)
members.thesis: Cointegrated stock pairs (stocks that share a long-run equilibrium despite short-term divergences) provide mean-reversion opportunities when their spread deviates from equilibrium. Unlike correlation, cointegration implies a stable long-run relationship. By applying the Johansen cointegration test t
entry_long: Spread_Zscore < -2.0 (spread significantly below equilibrium — long A, short B)
Spread_Zscore is not trending further down: Spread_Zscore > min(Spread_Zscore, last 10 bars)
entry_short: Spread_Zscore > 2.0 (spread significantly above equilibrium — short A, long B)
Spread_Zscore is not trending further up: Spread_Zscore < max(Spread_Zscore, last 10 bars)
members.exit_target: Spread_Zscore reverts to 0 (spread returns to equilibrium)
members.exit_stop: Spread_Zscore reaches -3.5 for long spread / +3.5 for short spread
filters: India VIX < 25; during high VIX, cointegration relationships may temporarily break
No entries before 09:30 (need 60 bars for spread statistics) or after 15:10
Both stocks must have volume > SMA(volume, 20) on entry bar
None — pairs trade is market-neutral by construction
weaknesses: Cointegration is a long-run property (typically tested on daily data over months/years) — testing on 20 days of 1-min data may detect spurious cointegration that is not economically meaningful
Two-legged execution doubles transaction costs (slippage and brokerage on both legs) and creates execution risk — if one leg fills and the other doesn't, you have unhedged directional exposure
Cointegration vectors (beta) estimated on historical data may drift within the session — if beta changes from 0.9 to 1.0, the spread signal is miscalibrated and entries may be premature
members.prior_art: Johansen (1991) cointegration test; Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) pairs trading; Vidyamurthy (2004) 'Pairs Trading'; intraday cointegration applications in Avellaneda & Lee (2010)
